speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in more detail, specifically regarding your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; are these symptoms constant or do they fluctuate in intensity?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fluctuating nature of your double vision and the worsening of weakness with activity that improves with rest strongly suggest a neuromuscular junction disorder. Do you experience any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis), difficulty swallowing, or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
